# @vllnt/convex-consent

> Append-only consent ledger (GDPR Art. 6/7) — record, withdraw, and gate consent per subject + purpose as a Convex component

`@vllnt/convex-consent` is a publishable Convex component. It targets `convex@^1.45.0`.
It stores two sandboxed tables. `consentEvents` is the append-only legal ledger (one immutable row per grant/deny/withdraw, never mutated — the GDPR proof — holding an opaque host `subjectRef`, a `purpose` key, a `decision` of `granted`/`denied`/`withdrawn`, the policy `version`, opaque host `proof`, and a server `at` timestamp). `consentState` is the derived current-decision projection — exactly one row per `(subjectRef, purpose)` — the O(1) runtime gate. A host mutation calls `record(ctx, subjectRef, purpose, decision, { version?, proof? })` (appends an event + updates the projection) or `withdraw(ctx, subjectRef, purpose, proof?)` (GDPR Art. 7(3) — appends a `withdrawn` event, but only when a grant is currently held, else throws `NO_CONSENT`/`NOT_GRANTED`). Before processing personal data the host calls `check(ctx, subjectRef, purpose, requiredVersion?)` — the gate — which returns `granted`/`stale` so a grant with an unequal policy `version` re-prompts; `getState`, `getStatesForSubject`, and paginated `history` read the record. Time is read from the server clock inside every handler — no caller-supplied clock. A bounded, self-rescheduling `prune` (and a built-in daily cron) sweeps all ledger events past the default 365-day retention window, including the current decision's evidence; the current-state projection is never pruned. The host owns the subject, the purpose meaning, auth, and the `proof` type (the client is generic over it, with an optional `proofValidator` parser narrowing the opaque stored value at the boundary — never a `v.any()` dump); the component owns only the consent record. Mount-safe: it runs correctly under multiple named `app.use` mounts.

Prune batch is 1–500 (default 200); invalid batch/cutoff throws INVALID_BATCH/INVALID_BEFORE. Custom sweeps cannot extend the built-in cron's retention. Host parsers are `(unknown) => T`, not `v.*.parse`. Legal compliance and evidence export remain host responsibilities.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in this package at `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-consent/docs/` and match the installed version. Read them, and the TypeScript source in `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-consent/src/`, before writing code that uses the package.
